# A filter that follows age


Older breasts are fattier, so fewer of their scans pass the fixed water threshold of 0.35 (@fig-usable-by-age). Here the
threshold instead follows the patient's age: 0.45 at age 30 and younger, falling in a straight line to
0.25 at age 60 and older. Patients without a recorded age keep the fixed threshold. The water centre rule is
unchanged.


::: {#cell-fig-dynamic-filter .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 8
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.8))

aged = [(nova_age[nova], height, usable(height, centre, dynamic_threshold(nova), CENTRE_MIN))
        for nova, _, _, _, height, centre in scan_records if nova in nova_age and np.isfinite(height)]
ages, heights, kept = (np.array(column) for column in zip(*aged))
ages = ages + rng.uniform(-0.4, 0.4, len(ages))
left.scatter(ages[~kept], heights[~kept], s=6, color=REJECTED_COLOUR, alpha=0.4, lw=0, label="rejected")
left.scatter(ages[kept], heights[kept], s=6, color="tab:purple", alpha=0.6, lw=0, label="kept")
age_line = np.linspace(ages.min() - 1, ages.max() + 1, 200)
left.plot(age_line, [threshold_at(a) for a in age_line], color="black", lw=1.8, label="age-dependent threshold")
left.axhline(WATER_MIN, color="black", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"fixed threshold ({WATER_MIN})")
left.set(xlabel="Age (years)", ylabel="Water peak height (stretched)", ylim=(0, min(1.2, np.nanmax(heights) * 1.05)))
left.grid(alpha=0.3)
left.legend(frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="none", fontsize=6.5, loc="upper right", markerscale=2)

width = 0.38
for i, comparison in enumerate(COMPARISONS):
    for j, (kind, (results, colour)) in enumerate(filters.items()):
        higher, total, p = results[comparison]
        x = i + (j - 0.5) * width
        share = higher / total if total else 0
        right.bar(x, share, width, color=colour, alpha=0.8, label=kind if i == 0 else None)
        right.text(x, share + 0.02, f"{higher}/{total}\np={p:.3f}" if total else "none", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=6)
right.axhline(0.5, color="black", ls=":", lw=1)
right.set_xticks(range(len(COMPARISONS)), [c.replace(" vs ", "\nvs ") for c in COMPARISONS])
right.set(ylim=(0, 1.15), ylabel="First-named breast has the higher Water:Fat")
right.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
right.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=6.5, loc="upper right")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

:::


Share of each age band's scans that each filter keeps:

| Filter | under 40 | 40–49 | 50 and over |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed | 67% | 50% | 24% |
| age-dependent | 57% | 51% | 35% |


CANCER vs NORMAL patients compared in each age band (first-named breast higher / compared):

| Filter | under 40 | 40–49 | 50 and over | no age |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixed | 1/2 | 8/9 | 3/4 | 3/3 |
| age-dependent | 1/2 | 8/9 | 6/10 | 3/3 |


The age-dependent filter keeps more of the older patients' scans and fewer of the youngest ones. That lets more patients be compared:
CANCER vs NORMAL goes from 15/18 \(83%\) (p = 0\.008) to
18/24 \(75%\) (p = 0\.023). All the new patients are 50 and
over, and they split about evenly: the band goes from 3/4 to
6/10. The stricter threshold for the youngest patients changes no comparison
under 40. So lowering the threshold to 0.25 for the oldest patients lets in scans fatty enough to hide the difference. BENIGN vs NORMAL and
CANCER vs BENIGN stay at or below chance with either filter.
